where: Wrackline Path and Lanternfall Road — the coastal road between Pearlmoor and the Vesper Crossroads, either side of the Sounding Cave
mood: Salt wind, last light — the coast road's pensive sibling: a longer, lonelier walk at dusk with the sea going dark beside you.
_note: Matches the classic mood sibling: 112 BPM, 4/4, E minor (relative minor of dimglass-coast-a's G). Unconditioned so the tempo holds. Contrast -a (bright springy 120 BPM first road): same sea air, but held yearning lead, rolling wave bass, airy pad, sparse brushes and shaker, still a travelling pulse.
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
yearning pulse-wave lead with long held notes reaching over the water
rolling plucked sampled bass rising and falling like waves
sparse harp arpeggios like distant buoys
soft brushed snare and a gentle shaker like sea foam washing in
long lonely coastal road at dusk, wistful, windswept, quietly brave

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {back on the road: the rolling wave bass and a soft shaker start walking on beat one, the wind pad breathes in, then the lead calls one long reaching note that leans into the theme}
styles: walking pulse from the first beat

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {the road melody in E minor, long held notes reaching out over dark water and settling back; wistful and hummable over the steady rolling bass}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the same melody again with a soft harp counter-line like buoy lights blinking, the pad a little wider, the brushes washing in like foam}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: the last light breaks through, a warmer turn to G major and C major, the lead lifts higher like a lantern seen far ahead, then the road bends back toward the minor}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the road melody returns in E minor, steady and walking; the last bar leads straight back into the main theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
